title: The road of fabrics and ideas
text: The Silk Road was never a single road, and silk was never its only cargo. For some 1,500 years a shifting {{1}} of routes linked China to the Mediterranean, and along them moved more than merchandise: Buddhism travelled to China this way, paper-making reached the Islamic world, and ideas about medicine, astronomy and mathematics {{2}} in both directions. What made the network {{3}} was geography — deserts, mountains and oases concentrated traffic into a handful of corridors where trading posts {{4}} into wealthy cities like Samarkand and Kashgar. No merchant travelled the whole distance: goods {{5}} through dozens of intermediaries, each adding a margin, which is why silk cost more than gold at the western end. The name itself is a nineteenth-century {{6}}, coined by a German geographer, and it {{7}} the sheer variety of what moved: glass, horses, spices, songs and diseases — the plague is thought to have reached Europe along these very routes. When sea transport matured, the land corridors {{8}} into memory. Their modern successors are being rebuilt by rail and pipeline, and archaeologists still dig caravan towns out of the sand.

gaps.explanation: 'a shifting network of routes' — an interconnected system; notion = idea, nurture = upbringing, nucleus = core.
'ideas flowed in both directions' — moved in a continuous exchange; float = drift aimlessly, flee = run away.
'What made the network possible was geography' — enabled it to exist; potent = powerful, porous = letting liquid through, positive = certain.
'trading posts grew into wealthy cities' — developed into; grope = feel about blindly, graze = feed on grass.
'goods passed through dozens of intermediaries' — moved from hand to hand; pace = walk at a speed, pave = surface a road.
'the name is a nineteenth-century invention' — it was coined, not ancient; inventory = a stock list, invasion = armed entry.
'it obscures the sheer variety of what moved' — hides it; obstruct = block the way, absorb = take in.
'the land corridors faded into memory' — gradually disappeared; fake = counterfeit, forge = counterfeit or forge ahead.
